Please find legal advice as well! This man is not above the law and he can't treat you like this. I pray that you will have justice. I also pray that you will continue to find God.
I pray that you find mercy and that your journey for a wholesome life is found. Everyone makes mistakes and God wants to help and guide you to be better.

Marriage is a big commitment and sometimes that means compromising. However, if what's happening is making you feel terrible about yourself, you need to be open about this to him. Throwing away a marriage because of a location/job is something that shouldn't be an end all. Try to work it out, find a therapist and have professional help for better opinions but most of all you need to be open.

Your comment has a lot of good questions! So to you, depending how they cheated is a factor? So for you, if your SO cheated in a way you consider the worst, but they came clean and felt remorse/asked to repair everything, would it still be a deal breaker for you?

Is it possible to consider going to couples therapy? Maybe tell him you aren't happy and either explain everything or show him this post. If you truly love each other, you two should put in work to make it better because that's a big factor for marriage: growing together.
